title: Warn before the lease expires; refuse runs on a stale athena binary
summary: Two guards for commands that run agents (audit, audience, drain, and the other callers of warn_if_stale). First, a warning on stderr when the operator lease (BRIEF.md:107) is close to expiring. Second, a refusal with the rebuild command when the installed binary is older than main, as `stale_build_line` already detects but today only prints. Each guard gets tests.

defaults_applied.how: Both checks get unit and CLI tests; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Criteria require tests that show a refused run and a printed warning, not just that the functions exist.
The refusal reuses the existing stale_build_line rule instead of adding a second staleness definition.
The stale-binary rule becomes a refusal in code rather than a printed advisory.
One focused change that adds a minimal lease reader only.
The outcome is a refused stale run and a warning before expiry, checked by tests.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: No lease exists in the code today: the only mention is BRIEF.md:107, the single-operator lease with the session and a since-time that expires. I assume 'its lease' means that lease, and that it is stored as a small record in the repository with an expiry time.
Because the lease has no implementation, the change adds a minimal lease reader. It does not add acquire/release machinery. A missing lease file produces no warning and no error.
The warning threshold is a constant (for example 10 minutes before expiry), or a field in athena.toml if the config pattern makes that cheap. I assume a constant, so athena.toml stays untouched.

'Main commit' is the repository HEAD that `Athena::stale_build` compares against. Staleness uses the existing definition (BUILD_PATHS changed since the binary's build commit), so docs-only commits do not block runs.

The refusal applies to the commands that call warn_if_stale today (audience, audit and the other two callers at main.rs:1041 and 1078), plus the agent-running paths of drain. Read-only commands such as status keep printing the line and still work.
An environment-variable or flag override for the refusal is out of scope, since it would defeat the guard. The error message names `./setup.sh` as the way out.
Audience is the project owner, who runs these commands and reads stderr. The tests are the criteria the verifier can run.
question: Which lease do you mean? The code has none. I assumed the single-operator lease in BRIEF.md:107, held as a repository record with an expiry.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test makes the installed binary's build commit older than HEAD by a commit that changes a file under crates/. It asserts that the audit command (and one other agent-running command) exits non-zero before any agent runs, with a message naming the build commit, HEAD and ./setup.sh. Run `cargo test`.

A test shows that a HEAD that differs from the build commit only by docs/ or records/ changes does not refuse the run (the existing stale-build rule is kept). A second test shows a build commit equal to HEAD is not refused. Run `cargo test`.

A unit test on the lease check, with an injected clock, shows a warning line when the remaining time is under the threshold, no warning when it is above, and a distinct 'expired' message when it has already passed. A missing lease gives neither a warning nor an error. Run `cargo test`.
A CLI-level test shows the lease warning is printed on stderr (not stdout, so --json output stays valid) by an agent-running command and does not stop that command. Run `cargo test`.
`cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean, and the existing test `status_prints_the_stale_build_line_after_a_crates_change_and_none_after_docs_or_records_changes` still passes.
CHANGELOG.md (Unreleased) records both checks. The code states which lease it reads and what the warning threshold is.

out_of_scope: Acquiring, renewing or releasing the lease, or any multi-session handoff logic
Automatically rebuilding or replacing the installed binary
An override flag to bypass the refusal
departures: The lease has no existing code, so the producer must design a minimal lease record. That adds cost and lowers acceptance and pass odds compared with the reference.
